wire.title: Kessel Valley line to close for six weeks of bridge repairs

paragraphs.text: The Kessel Valley railway line will close for six weeks from 3 November while engineers repair a damaged bridge near Harrow Bridge station, the operator said on Monday.
The line carries about 1,200 commuters a day between Harrow Bridge and the coast, and replacement buses will run every 20 minutes during the closure.
Kessel Rail said the bridge had been damaged by flooding in September and that inspections had found erosion around two of its supports.
The operator apologised for the disruption and said the work could not be put off without risking a longer closure in the depths of winter.
Season ticket holders will be offered a refund for the weeks the line is shut, the company said, with details to be published on its website.
Local MP Dana Whitlow said she had asked the transport department to make sure replacement services were accessible for disabled passengers.

wire.title: Fire guts Port Alder warehouse; twelve treated for smoke inhalation

paragraphs.text: A fire tore through a storage warehouse on the Port Alder industrial estate late on Sunday, sending a column of black smoke over the harbour and forcing the closure of two nearby roads.
Twelve people were treated for smoke inhalation after the fire at the Port Alder warehouse, officials said. None of the injuries were described as life-threatening.
At least 40 firefighters were sent to the scene from Port Alder and three neighbouring towns, and the blaze took 6 hours to bring under control.
The warehouse, owned by the logistics firm Brennock Freight, held packaging materials and household goods awaiting shipment to retailers across the region.
Residents within half a mile of the site were told to keep windows and doors closed overnight while crews dampened down hot spots.
Investigators have not yet said what caused the fire. A spokesperson for the regional fire service said an inquiry would begin once the building was declared safe to enter.
Harbour Road and Quay Lane remained closed on Monday morning, and the town council advised drivers to use the coast road instead.
Brennock Freight said in a statement that all of its staff on the night shift had been accounted for and thanked emergency crews for their response.

quiet.title: Why your afternoon coffee might be costing you sleep

paragraphs.text: Most adults should aim for seven to nine hours of sleep a night, yet surveys keep finding that a large share of us regularly get less than that.
Caffeine can stay in your system for up to six hours, which means a mid-afternoon coffee may still be working when you are trying to fall asleep.
Sleep researchers often describe caffeine as borrowing alertness from later in the day, because it blocks the chemical signal that builds up as you get tired.
Keeping a regular wake-up time, even at weekends, is one of the simplest habits for steadier sleep, and it costs nothing to try.
If you want to cut back, reduce your intake gradually over a week or two rather than stopping all at once, to avoid headaches.
